position.answer: John's 1846 marriage names his father John Glasgow, farmer, and the 1851 census proves his brother Samuel. Identification with the John in Nancy's notice is probable; extending the father to Alexander or identifying him with the flax grower remains unproved.
points: The father, John Glasgow, farmer (Glasgow-4090), is assessed at 98% from the 1846 marriage and the matching 1851 Lisnagaver household.
His death is probably the civil entry of 24 June 1885 at Lisnagaver, aged 78; the gravestone transcription's 1895 is probably an error for 1885.
The 1850 Drogheda sub-constable John Glasgow is not this man.
